arc-full-circle-ijk._why: Coincident endpoints with I/J/K is a full circle. Its chord is zero and it is emphatically not a zero-length move.

arc-helix._why: A helix: the third axis moves linearly across the arc, so the segment is longer than the planar arc by the rise.

arc-major-r._why: Negative R selects the major arc: the same endpoints, the long way round.

arc-plane-g17._why: The same quarter arc in G17. G18's handedness is the trap: RS-274 orders it Z then X so its normal is +Y, and reading it as X,Z turns every G2 into a G3.

arc-plane-g18._why: The same quarter arc in G18. G18's handedness is the trap: RS-274 orders it Z then X so its normal is +Y, and reading it as X,Z turns every G2 into a G3.

arc-plane-g19._why: The same quarter arc in G19. G18's handedness is the trap: RS-274 orders it Z then X so its normal is +Y, and reading it as X,Z turns every G2 into a G3.

arc-quarter-ijk._why: A quarter arc in centre-offset form. Paired with arc-quarter-r: the two must resolve to the same arc within 32 ULP, and their golden hashes are SUPPOSED to differ. See the corpus README.

arc-quarter-r._why: The same quarter arc in radius form. Positive R selects the minor arc.

arc-residual-within-tolerance._why: A centre 4 microns inconsistent between the endpoints, which is ordinary CAM rounding rather than an error. The centre is moved onto the chord's perpendicular bisector and the residual is recorded.

block-skip._why: A leading slash marks a block as optional, conditional on a control switch we do not have. The policy is a flag and is recorded in the IR header.

comment-forms._why: Both comment forms in one file, including an inline comment that must not swallow the words following it on the same line.

comment-unbalanced._why: An unbalanced parenthesis. Illegal, common in the wild, and a warning rather than a refusal because the file runs on the machine.

cycle-g73-g98._why: Peck whose chip-break retract is a machine parameter absent from the file. Without --chip-break-clearance the retract is omitted and counted in the header, so a collision check can refuse to certify against it. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g73-g99._why: Peck whose chip-break retract is a machine parameter absent from the file. Without --chip-break-clearance the retract is omitted and counted in the header, so a collision check can refuse to certify against it. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g81-g98._why: Drill: position, plunge to R, feed to depth, retract. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g81-g99._why: Drill: position, plunge to R, feed to depth, retract. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g82-g98._why: Drill with a dwell, which removes no material. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g82-g99._why: Drill with a dwell, which removes no material. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g83-g98._why: Peck with a full retract to the R plane between pecks. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g83-g99._why: Peck with a full retract to the R plane between pecks. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g84-g98._why: Tapping, which is geometrically a bore. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g84-g99._why: Tapping, which is geometrically a bore. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g85-g98._why: Bore: feed in, feed back out. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g85-g99._why: Bore: feed in, feed back out. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g86-g98._why: Bore with the spindle stopped: feed in, rapid out. G98 retracts to the initial Z, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-g86-g99._why: Bore with the spindle stopped: feed in, rapid out. G99 retracts to the R plane, which changes every intermediate retract in a pattern.

cycle-l0-does-nothing._why: L0 means do not execute. A real case, and one that reads exactly like a typo.

cycle-persists-until-g80._why: A cycle fires again on any block carrying axis words, and a block with only an F word does not fire it.

cycle-repeat-bolt-pattern._why: One line becomes a bolt pattern: L3 under G91 fires the cycle three times, each stepping by the same increment.

distance-incremental._why: G91: a delta is a delta in every frame, so incremental motion needs no offset chain at all.

feed-inverse-time._why: G93 inverse time: F is a reciprocal duration rather than a distance rate, so it must not be scaled by the unit factor. The norm in 5-axis output.

feed-per-revolution._why: G95 feed per revolution, which needs the spindle speed to become a duration.

motion-g28-two-moves._why: G28 travels to the reference point VIA an intermediate point given by the block's axis words. One straight move to the reference point can pass through the fixture.

offset-g10-mid-program._why: G10 L2 rewrites an offset that earlier segments already used. Their geometry is unaffected, but the header must record both epochs or a report rendering into a workpiece frame places the early moves wrongly.

offset-g53-machine-coordinates._why: G53 is non-modal and bypasses the work offset and the G92 shift for one block. It keeps tool length compensation, because the IR stores a tip position and a segment where 'tip' meant something else would trap U5.

offset-g54-to-g55._why: A mid-program work offset change. In machine coordinates the path stays continuous across it, which is the whole argument of ADR 0003.

offset-g92-shift._why: G92 is a persistent coordinate shift, not a move. Nothing travels on the G92 line itself.

reject-arc-ill-conditioned._why: An R-form arc sweeping almost exactly 180 degrees, where the centre is not determined by the endpoints. No tolerance rescues it.

reject-arc-r-full-circle._why: Coincident endpoints with an R word name no particular circle: every circle of that radius through the point qualifies.

reject-arc-radius-mismatch._why: A centre half a millimetre inconsistent between the endpoints, far beyond ordinary CAM rounding.

reject-cutter-comp-g41._why: G41 asks the control to offset the path by the tool radius, including lead-in and corner geometry that differs between controls. Simulating the uncompensated path would be wrong by the tool radius everywhere.

reject-g54-1._why: Fanuc's extended offsets are addressed by a P word and are a different mechanism. A range like 540..=593 would silently treat this as G54.

reject-heidenhain._why: Heidenhain Klartext, which is a different language rather than a dialect of RS-274 and is refused by name.

reject-macro-if._why: Flow control is macro programming: common in shop-written programs and absent from CAM output, so refusing it costs little and guessing costs much.

reject-macro-variable._why: Coordinates that come out of arithmetic the parser guessed at would make the verification meaningless.

reject-missing-decimal._why: On a legacy control X10 means 0.010 mm. A factor of a thousand that parses perfectly either way.

reject-modal-conflict._why: Two motion codes in one block. Which one a real control performs depends on the control, so there is no safe reading.

reject-no-feed-rate._why: A feed move before any F word has been commanded. Treating a missing feed as zero would divide by it later.

reject-o-word._why: LinuxCNC's procedural extension, not Fanuc RS-274. M98/M99 are supported.

reject-siemens-cycle._why: Siemens 840D is a different language, not a dialect. Refusing by name beats a syntax error at line 3.

reject-siemens-rparam._why: An R-parameter assignment. The `=` is what tells it from an arc radius.

reject-subprogram-recursion._why: A subprogram that calls itself would recurse until the stack gave out, which is a crash rather than a diagnosis.

reject-unknown-subprogram._why: M98 naming a body that does not exist. Falling through silently would run the wrong geometry rather than none.

reject-unsupported-code._why: G65 is a macro call, which needs the parametric evaluation this parser refuses. Naming it beats ignoring it.

subprogram-call._why: M98 calls a body and M99 returns. Execution stops at M30 rather than falling into the bodies that follow it.

units-change-mid-program._why: G20/G21 can change partway, and the change affects feed rates and offsets as well as coordinates.

note: Generated by scripts/gcode_corpus.py. `expect` is parse or reject; for a rejection, `error` is the GcodeError::kind() that must be produced. See README.md for the arc form amendment.
